clue.text: Wipe over new cab bonnet

indicators.note: the wiping word goes over, i.e. covers round, the other letters

parts.note: to wipe a floor is to mop it

indicators.note: new signals the letters of cab made afresh in another order

explanation.surface: Someone gives a freshly bought taxi's bonnet a wipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bonnet' suggests a car's engine cover; here it is a woman's cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A mob-cap is an old-fashioned frilled cloth cap, a kind of indoor bonnet worn by women.

clue.text: Love fine 8, say, in tiny new case, as one may well believe

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: in places the middle pieces within the shuffled letters
the shuffled letters act as a case holding the middle pieces
new signals the letters of tiny rearranged

parts.note: fine means good
the writer at 8 down is an example of an author

explanation.surface: A fussy description of a writer squeezed into a tiny new binding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges tiny to give letters split either side; 'in' and 'case' together put the fine author inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heard from a reliable source is information one may trust; the idiom means from a dependable informant.

clue.text: Leave no gaps for picture

definitions.meaning: to close ranks or shut the spaces between things
a photograph taken at very short range

explanation.surface: Advice to a photographer or a builder about spacing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means shut the spaces; the noun is a tightly framed photograph.

clue.text: Fruit brought round rest area — take it as it comes

indicators.note: the fruit is brought round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a pear is a fruit
a lay-by is a roadside parking spot where drivers rest

explanation.surface: A picnic in a roadside stop, with a laid-back shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: A lay-by is a British roadside pull-in for stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise without a plan, originally playing music without a score, is to deal with things as they arise.

clue.text: Poor Billy, regularly infested with moth

indicators.note: the picked letters are infested, i.e. filled, by the moth
regularly takes every other letter of Billy, the first, third and fifth

parts.note: an eggar is a type of moth

explanation.surface: Poor Billy finds his clothes riddled with moths.
explanation.walkthrough: The eggar is a large brown moth, less familiar than the clothes moth the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Beggarly means meagre or poverty-stricken, like a beggar; a synonym for poor.

clue.text: Panto character putting bum on seat, no worry

parts.note: butt is slang for bum, the backside
taken as written

indicators.note: no means the letters of the worrying word are absent from seat

parts.note: to worry is to eat at someone, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: Getting one's behind into a theatre seat without fretting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes EAT from SEAT, leaving S. Buttons is the page boy in the British Christmas pantomime Cinderella.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttons is the stock page boy role in pantomime Cinderella, a well-known stage figure.

clue.text: Caught lover's head in embrace, falling into ravine

indicators.note: in puts the small pieces inside the embrace word
in a down clue falling means the embrace word is read upwards

parts.note: an embrace is a hug

indicators.note: head takes the first letter of lover's

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A lover caught in a hug while tumbling into a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling' turns HUG into GUH; 'in' places L and C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulch is a narrow steep-sided valley, an American term for a gorge.

clue.text: Poisoner I contact, lacking ultimate drug

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: lacking ultimate drops the final letter of the contact word

parts.note: to contact someone is to ring them

explanation.surface: A poisoner gets in touch, minus his final ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkilling medicine, acetylsalicylic acid.

clue.text: She wrote automatically, so needing editing

indicators.note: editing reworks the letters of the two words into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer produced text without thinking, so it needed revising.
explanation.walkthrough: AUTOMATICALLY plus SO, rearranged, gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the American novelist who wrote Little Women, so a woman who wrote.

clue.text: Not aware Italian worker has lost son

indicators.note: has lost means the son letter is dropped

parts.note: signor is an Italian man, an Italian gentleman's title
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: An Italian labourer unaware his son has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant means lacking knowledge, an adjective for being unaware or uninformed.

clue.text: Eagerly accepts two drinks

parts.note: two drinks asks for a pair of drinking verbs; the first is lap, as a cat drinks
the second drinking verb is sup, to take small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly downs a pair of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two drinks' gives two verbs meaning drink, LAP and SUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap something up is an idiom for taking it in with enthusiasm, like praise.

clue.text: "Soft drink?", one snorts

definitions.meaning: a cola, the fizzy non-alcoholic kind
a slang name for cocaine, a powder taken through the nose

explanation.surface: A query about a fizzy beverage, met with a snort.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand name is a cola; the slang term is cocaine, which users snort.

clue.text: St Francis's body beginning to strengthen after long periods on soup

indicators.note: after means the first letter of strengthen comes at the end
on means the long periods follow the soup word

parts.note: broth is a thin soup
eras are long periods of time

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of strengthen

explanation.surface: A saint's body being built up on nourishing soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body' sounds like an organisation; it is the saint's own flesh, which he nicknamed after the humble donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: St Francis of Assisi called his own body by this name, treating the flesh as a humble beast of burden.

clue.text: Extract from record small, more than enough

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A short clip lifted from a recording, which is plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a sample is a snippet taken from an existing recording and reused.

clue.text: What family shares includes island country

indicators.note: includes means the island letter goes inside

parts.note: members of a family share a surname
I is a map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A family's common heritage includes an island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Suriname is a nation on the north coast of South America, formerly Dutch Guiana.

clue.text: Soundly interpreted character as special

indicators.note: soundly means the word for interpreted is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: to read a text or situation is to interpret it
a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: A character's role was sensibly performed as something special.
explanation.walkthrough: Past-tense READ is spoken like RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Festival days were marked in red on old calendars, so the term means memorable or notable.

clue.text: Fisherman's position on water's edge

parts.note: a stand is a position, as in taking a stand
re means on, in the sense of concerning

indicators.note: edge takes the first letter, the leading edge of water's

explanation.surface: An angler stationed at the waterside.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew the apostle was a fisherman before following Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Andrew, brother of Simon Peter, worked catching fish on Galilee.

clue.text: An Indian tune, popular, rises and falls

indicators.note: in a down clue rises means the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: a raga is a melodic form in Indian music
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: An Indian melody that soars and dips in popularity.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the US-Canada border, so falls is a name for it.

clue.text: Striker puts on women's jacket

indicators.note: puts on means the striker joins below the women letter in this down entry

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
one who raps or knocks is a rapper

explanation.surface: A footballer pulls on a lady's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapper is an outer covering, the jacket on a book or a sweet.

clue.text: Period in which court is closed: left on foot

indicators.note: on means the left letter follows
in which places the court inside the period
the period closes round the court, enclosing it

parts.note: a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A day when the court shuts, then off you go on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dactyl is a metrical foot in verse, one long syllable then two short ones.

clue.text: Fragments of music: A, E, and Cs

indicators.note: fragments signal the letters broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Snatches of a score listing the notes A, E and C sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cs' looks like more musical notes; it is the chemical symbol for the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesium is the soft alkali metal whose chemical symbol is Cs.

clue.text: Set of labels dotted about, bearing the same important title

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same
main means principal, important
a title is a name

explanation.surface: Scattered tags all carrying one grand heading.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet address is a series of labels separated by dots, like example.co.uk.

clue.text: No head wound without 18

indicators.note: no head drops the first letter of the winding word

parts.note: a road that wound its way has snaked

explanation.surface: A wound without a dressing, and no head injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury; it is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no covering or jacket is bare, i.e. lacking its outer layer.

clue.text: Slippers into which these go (not at the front)

indicators.note: not at the front drops the first letter

parts.note: feet, specifically heels, slide into slippers

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to put on house shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slippers' looks like footwear; it means slippery creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are notoriously slippery fish, so they are things that slip away.

clue.text: Make a grab: hello, sailor!

parts.note: hi is a greeting, hello
jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A greeting to a sailor before snatching something.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack is to seize a vehicle or plane by force, a sudden seizure.

clue.text: After exercise, got fit? Wrong to quibble

indicators.note: after means the shuffled letters come following the exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise

indicators.note: wrong signals the letters of got fit put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone back from the gym, arguing over whether they are fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To pettifog is to argue over trivial details, like a petty lawyer.

clue.text: In both hands, you may grasp smooth character from Athens

indicators.note: in puts the inner pieces within the two hands

parts.note: L and R are left and right, both hands

indicators.note: grasp means the you word holds the smooth word inside

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
to sand wood is to smooth it

explanation.surface: Holding something smooth in both hands, like a Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: Lysander is a young Athenian lover in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Lysander is one of the Athenian lovers in A Midsummer Night's Dream, a stage figure from Athens.

clue.text: Controller fitted with 5 down? Unlikely

definitions.meaning: a handset for a television, covered in push keys
as in a slim or faint chance

explanation.surface: Doubt whether a gadget comes with push keys.
explanation.definitionFit: The handheld TV control has keys; a faint or slight chance is called by the same word.
